recipes.title: Tacos al Pastor
recipes.dish_alt: Tacos al pastor topped with diced pineapple, onion, and cilantro on corn tortillas
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Marinated Pork on the Trompo
recipes.prep_alt: Achiote-marinated pork stacked on a vertical spit, the traditional al pastor trompo

sections.heading: Steps
items: Soak the dried guajillo chiles in boiling water 15 minutes until soft, then drain and remove stems and seeds.
Blend the softened chiles with achiote paste, pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, cumin, and oregano until smooth.
Coat the pork slices in the marinade and refrigerate at least 30 minutes.
Heat a skillet with a little oil over medium-high until shimmering.
Sear the pork in a single layer 3-4 minutes per side until deeply browned.
Chop the cooked pork into bite-sized bits.
In the same pan, caramelize the diced pineapple 1-2 minutes until golden-spotted.
Stir the chopped pork back in with the pineapple for 30 seconds.
Warm the corn tortillas about 20 seconds per side in a dry pan.
Pile the pork and pineapple onto warm tortillas, topped with onion, cilantro, and lime.

recipes.title: Chicken Enchiladas Verdes
recipes.dish_alt: Chicken enchiladas verdes topped with green salsa, crema, and crumbled queso fresco
recipes.prep_alt: Poached chicken breast shredded into thin strands for the enchilada filling

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Shredded Oaxaca or Monterey Jack cheese

sections.heading: Steps
items: Poach the chicken breast in gently boiling water 12-15 minutes until no pink remains.
Shred the cooled chicken into thin strips with two forks.
Husk and rinse the tomatillos, then boil with jalapeño and garlic 8-10 minutes until soft and olive-green.
Blend the tomatillos, jalapeño, garlic, onion, and cilantro until smooth into a salsa verde.
Simmer the salsa with the chicken stock 5 minutes until slightly darkened.
Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F).
Warm each tortilla in a little oil 5 seconds per side until pliable.
Fill each tortilla with shredded chicken, roll tightly, and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the salsa verde over the enchiladas, top with cheese, and bake 15-20 minutes until bubbling.
Drizzle with crema and crumbled queso fresco before serving.

recipes.title: Pozole Rojo (Pork & Hominy Soup)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of pozole rojo with shredded pork and hominy, topped with cabbage, radish, and lime
recipes.prep_alt: A bucket of dried maiz pozolero hominy corn at a Mexican market

sections.heading: Steps
items: Simmer the pork with a quarter of the onion, a garlic clove, and the bay leaf, skimming foam, 45-60 minutes until fork-tender.
Toast the stemmed, seeded chiles in a dry pan about 30 seconds per side until fragrant.
Soak the toasted chiles in boiling water 15 minutes until soft.
Blend the softened chiles with the remaining onion, garlic, and oregano, using soaking water to loosen. Strain.
Lift the tender pork out, shred or chop it, and discard the bay leaf.
Stir the strained red chile sauce into the broth.
Return the pork and hominy to the pot and simmer uncovered 20 minutes.
Taste and season with salt.
Ladle into bowls and set out cabbage, radish, and lime for topping.

recipes.title: Chiles Rellenos
recipes.dish_alt: Golden egg-battered chiles rellenos stuffed with melted cheese, served over tomato sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Poblano peppers charred and blistered over an open flame before peeling

sections.heading: Steps
items: Char the poblano peppers directly over a flame or under a broiler until blackened all over, about 8-10 minutes.
Steam the charred peppers in a covered bowl 10 minutes, then rub off the blackened skin.
Slit each pepper, scoop out the seeds and membrane, and stuff with cheese.
Simmer the onion and garlic in oil 2-3 minutes, then add crushed tomatoes and stock, simmering 10 minutes for the sauce.
Beat the egg whites to soft peaks, then gently fold in the yolks to make a fluffy batter.
Roll each stuffed pepper in flour, then dip and coat fully in the egg batter.
Fry the battered peppers in hot oil 3-4 minutes, turning gently, until golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towels.
Spoon the warm tomato sauce onto plates and top with a chile relleno to serve.

recipes.title: Tinga de Pollo (Smoky Chipotle Chicken Tostadas)
recipes.dish_alt: Crisp tostadas piled with smoky chipotle chicken tinga, lettuce, avocado, and queso fresco
recipes.prep_alt: Canned chipotle peppers in smoky adobo sauce, the base of the tinga sauce

sections.heading: Steps
items: Poach the chicken in gently boiling water 12-15 minutes until no pink remains, then shred with two forks.
Blend the tomatoes, chipotle peppers, and adobo sauce until mostly smooth.
Cook the onion in a little oil 3-4 minutes until soft, then add garlic for 30 seconds.
Pour in the tomato-chipotle sauce and chicken stock, simmering 8-10 minutes until thickened.
Add the shredded chicken and stir to coat, simmering 5 more minutes.
Taste and season with salt.
Pile the tinga onto crisp tostadas.
Top with shredded lettuce, sliced avocado, and crumbled queso fresco.

recipes.title: Carne Asada
recipes.dish_alt: Sliced grilled carne asada tacos with tortillas, cilantro, onion, and pico de gallo
recipes.prep_alt: Citrus-marinated skirt steak, arrachera-style, searing on a hot grill

sections.heading: Steps
items: Whisk together lime juice, orange juice, garlic, olive oil, cumin, and half the cilantro.
Marinate the steak in the citrus mixture at least 30 minutes, up to 4 hours.
Let the steak sit out 15 minutes before cooking so it isn't ice-cold.
Heat a grill or grill pan over high heat until very hot.
Grill the steak undisturbed 3-4 minutes per side until well marked.
Flip once and cook 3-4 minutes more for medium doneness.
Rest the steak 5-10 minutes before slicing.
Slice thinly against the grain.
Serve with warm tortillas, grilled onion, cilantro, and pico de gallo.

recipes.title: Pollo en Mole Poblano
recipes.dish_alt: Chicken simmered in rich, dark mole poblano sauce, sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds
recipes.prep_alt: Dried ancho chiles, the base of the deep, complex mole poblano sauce

sections.heading: Steps
items: Toast the stemmed, seeded ancho and pasilla chiles in a dry pan 20-30 seconds per side.
Soak the toasted chiles in boiling water 15 minutes until soft.
Toast the almonds and sesame seeds separately until golden, setting a pinch of sesame aside for garnish.
Cook the onion and garlic in a little oil until soft, then add tomato and cook until saucy.
Blend the soaked chiles, toasted nuts and seeds, onion-tomato mixture, raisins, and half the stock until smooth.
Cook the thick paste in a pot, stirring often, 5 minutes until darkened and toasty.
Stir in the rest of the stock until the sauce is smooth and pourable.
Add the chicken thighs, cover partway, and simmer 25-30 minutes until fully cooked.
Melt the chocolate into the sauce and simmer 5 more minutes.
Spoon over rice and sprinkle with the reserved toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Churros with Mexican Chocolate Sauce (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: Cinnamon-sugar dusted churros served with warm Mexican chocolate dipping sauce
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Piping and Frying the Dough
recipes.prep_alt: Ridged churro dough being piped and fried to golden brown at a Mexico City market stall

sections.heading: Steps
items: Bring water, butter, sugar, and salt to a boil until the butter melts.
Off the heat, stir in all the flour at once until it forms a smooth dough ball.
Let the dough cool about 5 minutes.
Beat in the egg a little at a time until smooth and glossy.
Pipe the dough into a piping bag fitted with a star tip.
Heat the oil to about 190°C (375°F).
Pipe 10-13cm lengths of dough directly into the hot oil, a few at a time.
Fry 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp, then drain on paper towels.
Roll the warm churros in cinnamon sugar.
Warm the milk, stir in the chopped chocolate until melted, and serve alongside for dipping.
